o1.biggest_strength: It acts on the real signal in the data: protect migration first, put creators and extension authors ahead of Product Hunt, and stage the rollout so support does not get crushed again.
o1.biggest_mistake: The channel table says it is ranked by week-4 share rather than retained users, which could confuse the decision even though the actual launch order is right for us.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the retained-user ranking language, confirm the staged rollout mechanics, and move the final migration go/no-go earlier than the code freeze or split it into pre-freeze and launch gates.

o2.biggest_strength: It catches the main lesson from the last launch: hotkeys and settings are the launch risk, while creators and extension authors are the highest-quality acquisition channels.
o2.biggest_mistake: It creates avoidable launch-day load by emailing 420,000 users and posting to Show HN on day one while also claiming a staged rollout; it also assumes engineers can join support during freeze.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Separate existing-user waves from broad launch noise, push HN/Product Hunt later, remove placeholders, and make the support and beta-testing plan fit the small team more realistically.

reason: I would rather run Output 1. It is closer to an operating plan: it stages risk, uses the community asset well, keeps PH/HN in their place, and the copy is nearly publishable.
